correctness.rationale: The ball Fourier formula, exact angular kernel, and fixed-order Bessel asymptotics establish the uniform R^{d+1} scaled expansion with cross term O(R^{-(d-1)/2}). Compact-torus annihilator theory identifies every possible asymptotic phase vector; finite cosine-zero classes give an exact quantified arithmetic test. The rank-one relation lattice for coprime two-ball ratios yields the divisibility threshold, and differentiation of an explicit periodic trigonometric polynomial gives the radical coefficient. All dimensions, endpoints, and irrational cases follow analytically; finite code only checks transcription and normalization.

value.rationale: For the natural first disconnected smooth component model, the generic sharp upper R^{-d-1} decay does not distinguish isolated spectral zeros from a uniform positive lower floor. This finding resolves that distinction for every finite ball union by rational relations, gives a precise modulo-four two-component phase transition across dimensions, and supplies an exact sharp planar ratio-1:2 coefficient. These are structural and intrinsically useful for frequency-resolved Fourier energy, not an arbitrary finite enumeration.
